# Uuid

A universally unique identifier: sixteen bytes in the standard's own order.

```rux
pub struct Uuid {
    pub bytes: byte[N];
}
```

## Fields

| Name    | Type      | Description                                |
| ------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `bytes` | `byte[N]` | The sixteen bytes, most significant first. |

## Associated functions

<h3 id="nil"><code>Nil</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Nil() -> Uuid
```

The nil UUID: sixteen zero bytes.
A defined value rather than an absence, and worth having as one — the alternative is every caller
inventing a sentinel of their own.

**Returns**: the all-zero value

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L39)

<h3 id="max"><code>Max</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Max() -> Uuid
```

The max UUID: sixteen bytes of ones, which RFC 9562 defines as nil's counterpart.

**Returns**: the all-ones value

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L47)

<h3 id="from-bytes"><code>FromBytes</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FromBytes(bytes: byte[..]) -> Uuid
```

A UUID from sixteen bytes in the standard's order.
Fewer than sixteen leaves the rest zero; more are ignored. No structure is imposed — the version and
variant fields are whatever the bytes say, which is what lets this read a UUID from somewhere else.

| Name    | Type       | Description                                             |
| ------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bytes` | `byte[..]` | sixteen bytes to take as the value, in big-endian order |

**Returns**: those sixteen bytes as a value, with no field interpreted or corrected

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L63)

<h3 id="version"><code>Version</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Version(self: &Uuid) -> uint8
```

The version, from the high nibble of the seventh byte.
Meaningful only for the standard variant; a nil or max UUID reports a number that means nothing, which
is why [`Variant`](/docs/api/uuid/uuid#variant) should be consulted first.

**Returns**: the version nibble, 0 through 15; a value this package did not make may hold anything

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L109)

<h3 id="variant"><code>Variant</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Variant(self: &Uuid) -> UuidVariant
```

The variant, from the high bits of the ninth byte.
The encoding is variable-length rather than two fixed bits: a leading zero means the oldest layout, `10`
the standard one, `110` Microsoft's, and `111` the reserved future.

**Returns**: the variant the layout declares

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L118)

| `other` | `&Uuid` | the value to compare against |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L130)

<h3 id="compare"><code>Compare</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Compare(self: &Uuid, other: &Uuid) -> Ordering
```

Orders two UUIDs by their bytes, most significant first.
For a version 7 UUID this is chronological order, because its timestamp occupies the leading bytes in
big-endian form. Reordering here — to match a platform's GUID layout, say — would destroy that, which
is why the byte order is fixed rather than negotiable.

| Name    | Type    | Description                  |
| ------- | ------- | ---------------------------- |
| `other` | `&Uuid` | the value to compare against |

**Returns**: how the two order as sixteen big-endian bytes, which is lexicographic order for the text

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L146)

<h3 id="hash"><code>Hash</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Hash(self: &Uuid) -> uint64
```

A hash of the sixteen bytes, for use as a table key.
FNV-1a, which is not a cryptographic hash and does not need to be: a UUID is already the output of one,
or of an entropy source, so what a table wants here is speed and an even spread over buckets.

**Returns**: the value's hash

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L161)

## Implements Display

`Uuid` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &Uuid,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the canonical lower-case form, or the URN form under the `urn` style.
The default is the hyphenated form RFC 9562 defines, in lower case, because that is the one representation
the standard has and the one every other implementation writes. `hyphenated` names it explicitly and `urn`
selects the `urn:uuid:` form. Upper case is not a style, since a canonical form that varies by case is not
canonical; [`FormatUpper`](/docs/api/uuid/text#format-upper) remains for a format that demands it.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for any other style or for a precision, which
a value of exactly one length has nothing to apply.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole form was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L265)

## Related

<h3 id="swap-guid-order"><code>SwapGuidOrder</code></h3>

```rux
pub func SwapGuidOrder(value: &Uuid) -> Uuid
```

The same identifier with its first three fields byte-swapped, which is how Windows stores a GUID.
The conversion is its own inverse, so one function serves both directions: a UUID becomes the GUID bytes a
Windows API expects, and GUID bytes read from one become the UUID they represent. It must be called
deliberately — applying it by accident, or failing to apply it when crossing the boundary, both produce a
well-formed identifier that refers to something else entirely.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Random.rux#L52)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description         |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------- |
| `value` | `&Uuid` | the value to act on |

**Returns**: the same sixteen bytes with the first three fields byte-swapped

<h3 id="uuid-variant"><code>UuidVariant</code></h3>

```rux
pub enum UuidVariant: int32 {
    NetworkComputingSystem = 0,
    Standard = 1,
    Microsoft = 2,
    Future = 3
}
```

What layout a UUID's bytes follow.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Uuid/Src/Uuid.rux#L22)

**Cases**

| Name                     | Value | Description                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NetworkComputingSystem` | `0`   | Apollo NCS, from before the standard — the layout the nil UUID also happens to match. |
| `Standard`               | `1`   | The layout RFC 9562 defines, which is what essentially every UUID in use is.          |
| `Microsoft`              | `2`   | Microsoft's early variant: reserved, and rare.                                        |
| `Future`                 | `3`   | Reserved for the future and never assigned.                                           |
